title: `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`'s `owd_widening_forbidden` row rationalizes its pending registration from a wire shape the live route does not produce (`code` vs `declaredCode`)
body:
Filed by the `domain:services` seat (session `session_01PnJHU45vPJj5UQrxe946Bx`) from #9477's accepted measurement — the dev's out-of-scope finding, filed by the accepting seat per protocol. Unassigned, unlabelled for triage (landing file `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` is cli-lane territory; the ADR-0112 registration question it feeds may pull spec).

## The mismatch

The `owd_widening_forbidden` row (verdict `pending-registration`) justifies itself with: the refusal "reaches the wire verbatim" and `meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts` "reads a 403 body whose `code` is this string".

Measured on the live REST route (#9477, verbatim capture in its `<!-- os-dev-report -->`): the wire answers

```json
{"code": "PERMISSION_DENIED", "declaredCode": "owd_widening_forbidden", ...}
```

— the token reaches the wire in `declaredCode`, not `code`. The unit pin (`packages/rest/src/meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts`) reads the in-process shape, which is where the bare spelling lives; the ledger row's reachability rationale describes a wire form the route does not produce.

## Why it matters

The row is `pending-registration` under ADR-0112 — the decision whether/how to register this code should be made from the true wire shape (a `declaredCode` carrier under a standard-catalog `code`), not from the rationale as written. Consumers keying on `code` alone MISS this refusal today (PR #9953's checklist revision now warns runners about exactly that).

## Fix shape (a lead)

Correct the row's `why` to the measured two-field shape, and let the pending ADR-0112 registration decision consume the corrected fact. Whether `declaredCode`-carried tokens need their own registration lane is the spec-side half of that decision — not prejudged here.

Re-check commands: `git grep -n "owd_widening_forbidden" origin/main -- packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` · the wire capture in #9477's report.

Refs: #9477 · #9567 (the closed card that created the row) · #9460 (the sweep gap that preceded it) · ADR-0112.
